# EDAlign

> A Go implementation of the sequence alignment library [edlib](https://github.com/Martinsos/edlib) with added support for SIMD acceleration



### Usage

```go
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"github.com/microbiotica/edalign"
)

func main() {
	// Create a default configuration.
	// The default configuration uses IUPAC alternative equalities and extracts only the edit distance
	var config = edalign.DefaultConfig()

	// Transform the target and query sequence into the target Alphabet
	var (
		query  = config.Alphabet.Transform(``)
		target = config.Alphabet.Transform(``)
	)

	// Perform the alignment
	result, err := edalign.Align(query, target, config)
	if err != nil {
		// do something with err
	}

	// Do something with the result
	fmt.Printf("Edit Distance: %d\n", result.EditDistance)
	fmt.Printf("Percent Identity: %.2f%%\n", result.PercentIdentity)
}

```
### SIMD acceleration

On amd64, alignment uses AVX-512 or AVX2 column kernels when the CPU supports them, detected at runtime.
On arm64 (including Apple silicon), alignment uses an assembly column kernel that runs on every arm64 CPU.
Other platforms and CPUs use the portable implementation. All produce identical results.

- Build with `-tags purego` to compile only the portable implementation.
- Set `GODEBUG=cpu.avx512f=off` to use AVX2 instead of AVX-512, or `GODEBUG=cpu.avx2=off,cpu.avx512f=off` to use the portable implementation.

Compare the implementations with `go test -run xxx -bench Implementations`.
